artist_en: Yilin Luo, Xuanyi Zhang, Jianwei Yang, Qiushi Zhou
artist_cn: 罗伊琳，张轩逸，杨剑玮，周秋实
description_en:
When you step before the mirror, you do not see yourself clearly. Your reflection is there — but over it, constituting it, is a point cloud: the tracking system's rendering of your body as discrete spatial data. You appear first as the mirror has already processed you, not as light returning from glass but as coordinates in a computational space. The technical apparatus does not hide itself. It surfaces first.  

Then a sphere appears, floating. It is positioned so that your point cloud can occlude it — reach toward it and the visual overlap is real. Something responds. This is the first discovery: your data-body has weight in this space.  As you move, the world emerges. A fantastical natural environment grows out of the geometric skeleton — plant-animal hybrid forms, translucent structures that are flower and fish simultaneously, metallic-organic branches that look like both skeleton and living tissue. The world does not pre-exist your presence. It is generated by it.  

And as the world appears, your technical self recedes. The point cloud dissolves. By the time the environment is fully present, what you see in the mirror is only your optical reflection — continuous, analog, the body as light — moving through a world it called into being. The data-body has been absorbed. What began as apparatus has become milieu.  Before you leave, a flower — generated by your interaction with the mirror — waits by the exit. It is the one thing the mirror lets you take --- a tertiary retention made portable: the technical memory of your encounter.  

《共生》 stands at another location on campus. It is not a replica of the mirror experience. It is what the mirror's world looks like when it has detached from the glass and the body both — the same individuating forms, encountered without the interaction that made them. You may find it before or after the mirror. Either way, it has already been waiting.
description_cn:
站在镜前，你看到的并非清晰的自己。你的倒影在那里，但在它之上，与它共同构成它的，是一团点云：追踪系统对你身体的渲染，将你呈现为离散的空间数据。你最初以镜子已经处理过你的方式出现——不是光从玻璃上返回，而是计算空间中的一组坐标。技术装置并不隐藏自己，它率先浮现。  

随后，一个球体出现，悬浮在前。它的位置经过设计，使你的点云恰好能够遮挡它——向它伸手，视觉上的重叠是真实的。有什么东西回应了。这是第一个发现：你的数据之身，在这个空间里有重量。  
随着你的移动，世界开始浮现。一个奇幻的自然环境从几何骨架中生长而出——植物-动物混合形态，半透明的结构同时是花也是鱼，金属-有机的枝干既像骨骼也像活体组织。这个世界并非预先存在，它由你的在场所生成。  

而随着世界的显现，你的技术性自我也逐渐隐退。点云消散。当环境完全呈现时，你在镜中看到的只剩下你的光学倒影——连续的、模拟的、身体作为光的存在——在一个由它自身召唤而出的世界中移动。数据之身已被吸收。最初作为装置存在的东西，已成为环境。离开之前，一朵由你与镜子的互动所生成的花，在出口处等待着你。那是镜子允许你带走的唯一之物 --- 那是一份可携带的第三持留：你此次相遇的技术记忆。

《共生》驻立在校园的另一处空间。它不是镜中体验的复制。它是镜子的世界脱离了玻璃与身体之后的形态——同样的个体化形式，在没有生成它们的那场互动的情况下被遭遇。你可能在遇见镜子之前先遇见它，也可能在之后。无论如何，它一直在那里等待。
artist_bio_en:
Qiushi Zhou is an Assistant Professor at Computational Media and Arts Thrust and Internet of Things Thrust of Information Hub at HKUST (GZ). With broad interest in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Qiushi’s research focuses on building and understanding fundamental interaction techniques for future XR interfaces. The main themes of his work include novel eye+hand input techniques in XR, creative use of augmented mirrors in both practical and artistic contexts, and theoretical and historical reflections on interaction design concepts and paradigms. Qiushi serves as Program Committee and Editorial Board members for top HCI venues, including CHI, UIST, and ISS. He has collaborated with global industry leaders in XR, including Google, Meta, and Logitech, and with renowned artists to build interactive installations exhibited at galleries and festivals in Australia.

Yilin and Xuanyi are students of Dr. Qiushi Zhou. Their research interests lie in exploring new interaction methods.
artist_bio_cn:
罗伊琳是学习交互艺术的学生。她的研究兴趣集中在人机交互（HCI）领域，尤其关注与镜子相关的扩展现实交互。她探索如何将反射表面重新构想为交互界面，并研究其在扩展现实环境中重塑感知、身体感与空间交互的潜力。

张轩逸是香港科技大学（广州）计算媒体与艺术（CMA）学域的博士研究生。经由横跨艺术策展与数字媒体的学术背景，其研究立足于人机交互、技术哲学及批判性媒体研究的交汇点。他的研究旨在对弥散于当代生活的各类技术物展开批判性探究，并将这些技术系统视为蕴含丰富文化、社会及哲学意涵的关键场域。通过整合上述跨学科领域，他致力于探索人类与其所栖居的技术环境之间那些微妙而复杂的关系。

杨剑玮目前是暨南大学硕士研究生，研究兴趣包括人机交互、扩展现实与虚拟现实交互技术。他主要关注沉浸式环境中的交互方式设计、用户行为分析与用户体验评估。

周秋实是香港科技大学（广州）信息枢纽计算媒体与艺术学域以及物联网学域的助理教授。他对人机交互（HCI）有广泛的兴趣，研究重点是给未来的扩展现实（XR）界面构建基础性的交互技术。
他的主要研究主题包括：XR中结合眼动与手部输入的新型交互技术、增强镜在实用与艺术语境中的创新应用，以及对交互设计概念与范式的理论与历史反思。
他曾担任多个人机交互顶级会议（包括CHI、UIST和ISS）的程序委员会成员及期刊编委。他还与全球XR行业领军企业（包括Google、Meta和Logitech）开展合作，并与知名艺术家合作打造互动装置作品，这些作品曾在澳大利亚的画廊与艺术节中展出。

description_en: ASTRA is a Mixed Reality Experience that transports you from Earth to the deepest corners of the cosmos as you embark on a quest to uncover the key ingredients of life in the Universe. Step foot on planets and their dark moons in a search for future worlds and far away beings.
description_cn: 欢迎来到 ASTRA——通往群星的门票。这一混合现实体验将带你从地球出发，前往宇宙最深处，踏上一场寻找宇宙中生命关键要素的旅程。你将踏足行星及其幽暗的卫星，探索未来世界与遥远生命存在的可能。
artist_bio_en: Eliza McNitt is a writer and director. She is an Emmy Awards Finalist and recipient of the VR Grand Prize at The Venice Film Festival. She explores the cosmic collision of science and art. From astronauts to astrophysicists, McNitt works alongside scientists to tell stories about the human connection to the cosmos.  Her VR experiences have appeared at Sundance, SXSW, AFI Fest, Cannes NEXT, Tribeca, Telluride, and Venice. She’s a two time Intel Science Fair winner, Alfred P. Sloan grant recipient, and Gold Screen Young Director's Award winner at Cannes Lions.
artist_bio_cn: Eliza McNitt 是一位编剧兼导演，曾入围艾美奖，并获得威尼斯电影节 VR 单元大奖。她的创作探索科学与艺术在宇宙尺度上的交汇，并长期与宇航员、天体物理学家等科学家合作，讲述人类与宇宙之间的联结。她的 VR 作品曾亮相 Sundance、SXSW、AFI Fest、Cannes NEXT、Tribeca、Telluride 与 Venice 等电影节。

description_en:
Riding on the back of a giant turtle, you are invited to descend into a submerged reimagination of Shek Kip Mei Park as an underwater dreamscape, built from memories of this now demolished Hong Kong landmark. Once nestled along the foothills of Lion Rock, the park’s walkways, pastel-tiled fountain, and pavilions now appear as drifting aquatic ruins, illuminated by shifting blue light. The turtle serves as your guide through this sunken world meditative form of movement. In this imagined underworld, reality and fiction blend: the silent fountain, once the largest artificial waterfall in Hong Kong, rests like a relic suspended in time. The transformation adds a surreal experience to the digital preservation, a unique atmosphere and sensory presence that once defined the site.
The artwork grew from an effort to document the park before its removal, combining artistic interpretation with digital reconstruction. Several techniques were tested and ultimately fused to form the final environment. LiDAR scanning captured the overall spatial geometry, producing abstract but accurate point-cloud structures. Photogrammetry provided detailed meshes for architectural elements, ensuring stability and clarity for VR immersion. Gaussian splatting (3DGS) was explored for intricate textures and organic forms; while effective in small areas, it proved challenging for largescale scenes and was used selectively.
By merging these approaches, the project creates a hybrid digital twin: an abstract structural shell punctuated by pockets of realism and surreality. This balance reflects both the site’s heritage and its gradual decay, offering a space where users can rediscover a vanished environment through an evocative underwater journey. The result is simultaneously an accurate reconstruction and an atmospheric reimagination of the place, merely an invitation to drift through memory, myth, and loss on the back of a giant turtle.

UE artists: Benjamin Seide, Zhang Tianyi (Tony), Timothy Koo
3D modelling: Zhong Hui
LiDAR scanning and drone recording: Fong Hin Nam and Chan Hoi Tat, Ben
Sound: Ross Williams
Narrative: Sebastian Pelz
description_cn:
骑乘巨龟之背，您被邀请进入石硖尾公园的水下重构世界，这里被重新构想为一片水下梦境，由这座现已拆除的香港地标建筑的影像记忆所构建而成。这座公园曾依偎在狮子山山麓，其步道、粉彩瓷砖喷泉和凉亭如今化作漂浮的水下遗迹，在变幻的蓝光中若隐若现。龟在这个沉没的世界中引导您，以冥想般的流动动作穿行。在这个想象中的地下世界里，现实与虚构交融：那座曾经是香港最大人工瀑布的静默喷泉，如今宛如一件悬停于时间中的遗迹。这种转化赋予了数字保存一种超现实的体验，营造出一种独特的氛围与感官存在感，这正是曾经定义该场所的特质。

该艺术作品源于对公园拆除前进行记录的尝试，将艺术诠释与数字重建相结合。经过对多种技术的测试，最终将它们融合在一起，形成了最终的环境。LiDAR激光雷达扫描捕捉了整体的空间几何结构，生成了一系列抽象但精确的点云结构。摄影测量技术为建筑构件提供了精细的网格模型，确保了虚拟现实沉浸体验的稳定性和清晰度。高斯溅射（3DGS）技术被用于处理复杂的纹理和有机形态；虽然在小范围内效果明显，但在大规模场景中遇到挑战，因此选择性使用。

通过融合这些方法，该项目创造了一个混合型数字孪生体：一个抽象的结构外形，其中点缀着现实主义与超现实主义的片段。这种平衡既体现了该遗址的历史传承，也映射出其渐趋衰败的现状，为用户提供了一个空间，让他们能通过一场引人入胜的水下旅程，重新发现那个已然消逝的环境。最终成果既是对该场所的精准复原，也是对其氛围的重新构想，更是一份邀请，骑着巨龟徜徉于记忆、神话与失落之间。

artist_bio_en:
Benjamin Seide is a media artist, researcher, and educator at the School of Art, Design and Media, NTU Singapore. His research explores innovative uses of VR and advanced technologies for the artistic interpretation of cultural heritage. His work has been exhibited at V&A Digital Futures (London), Beyond Future Design Festival (ZKM Karlsruhe), and the Palais des Nations (Geneva). As a visual effects specialist, he contributed to award-winning films by Wim Wenders, Roman Polanski, J.J. Abrams, and Martin Scorsese’s Hugo (Academy Award for Best Visual Effects), and received Emmy honours for Game of Thrones.
www.ataribaby.de

Elke Reinhuber is Associate Professor at the School of Creative Media, City University of Hong Kong for Expanded Photography. Her artistic research explores sustainability, emerging technologies, and cultural heritage. Before moving to Hong Kong, she taught and conducted research internationally, including at NTU Singapore’s School of Art, Design and Media, GUC Cairo, and the University of the Arts Braunschweig in Germany. She graduated from UDK Berlin and earned her PhD from UNSW Sydney for her exploration on choice, decision making, and counterfactuals in media arts. Her award-winning work has been presented internationally at leading institutions and major conferences.
www.eer.de
artist_bio_cn:
Benjamin Seide 本宸瑋是一位媒体艺术家、研究者及新加坡南洋理工大学艺术、设计与传媒学院的教育者。他的研究探索虚拟现实和先进技术在文化遗产艺术解读中的创新应用。他的作品曾在伦敦的V&A维多利亚与阿尔伯特博物馆数字未来展、卡尔斯鲁厄ZKM的超越未来设计节以及日内瓦的联合国欧洲总部展出。作为视觉特效专家，他参与了温·温德斯、罗曼·波兰斯基、J.J.艾布拉姆斯的获奖电影制作，并为马丁·斯科塞斯的《雨果》贡献了特效，该片获得了奥斯卡最佳视觉效果奖，同时还因《权力的游戏》获得艾美奖荣誉。
www.ataribaby.de

Elke Reinhuber 莱因胡伯是香港城市大学创意媒体学院的副教授，专注于扩展摄影的领域。她的艺术研究涉及可持续性、新兴技术与文化遗产。在来到香港之前，她曾在国际上教学和从事研究，包括在新加坡南洋理工大学的艺术、设计与传媒学院、开罗德国大学和德国布伦瑞克艺术大学。她毕业于柏林艺术大学，获得新南威尔士大学的博士学位，研究主题为媒体艺术中的选择、决策和反事实探讨。她的获奖作品已在国际顶尖机构和大型会议上展出。
www.eer.de

description_en:
Bug in My Software (BIMS) is a real-time simulation paired with handmade textile installation that reimagines artificial intelligence along the biological, cultural, and industrial history of silk production. The project is centered on the silkmoth (Bombyx mori), one of the earliest lifeforms redesigned by human intervention. In BIMS, silkmoth DNA, reproductive cycle, and labor role become the blueprint for a real-time synthetic ecosystem populated by evolving digital agents. Situating AI within the history of textile labor, biological engineering, and industrial automation, BIMS reframes machine intelligence as collective, biological, and materially entangled. 

The system runs as a continuously evolving simulation in which artificial silkmoths inhabit, mutate, adapt to, and interact with each other and their simulated speculative ecosystem. The visual environment behaves as a hybrid between an ecological terrarium and a computational substrate, in which digital organisms evolve over long-form interaction cycles. This ecology does not respond to discrete user commands: rather than consumption of a user-controlled interface, the installation frames the viewing experience as “field observation” of a xenobiological AI.

Beyond simulation, the project includes a material archive: hand-woven textile encoding real silkmoth DNA sequences placed on the floor. The textile serves as a symbolic dataset - palimpsest of human intervention into the species - with the patterns informing the visual grammar of the simulation. 

Though the textile’s design is informed by converting DNA sequence into a visual color-coded field via algorithmic processes, its materiality and construction are the result of manual, repetitive labor, performed by the artist over several months. This
juxtaposition of handcraft and computational automation highlights the dynamics of hidden labor behind both traditional and digital production systems.

Lastly, BIMS reframes the immersive experience as an embodied physical encounter, as the visitors are invited to engage with the textile, to sit, recline, embed (or re-embed) themselves into the speculative ecosystem while contemplating its digital landscape.
description_cn: 《Bug in My Software》是一件沉浸式混合装置，探索有机体与工程系统、劳动与自动化之间的关系。作品以家蚕蛾（Bombyx Mori）为核心——这一物种在历史上曾被人类为丝绸生产而驯化与改造。项目将由蚕蛾 DNA 衍生出的纺织景观，与实时运行的推想性生态系统模拟交织在一起。观众通过 XR 头显与屏幕，与不断演化的数字昆虫——蚕蛾、蚕以及它们所处的生态系统——发生互动，见证不可预测的互动与转化。通过将手工技艺与算法设计相结合，《Bug in My Software》以诗意的混合景观揭示隐藏的劳动，并呈现人类与非人类智能之间日益模糊的边界。
artist_bio_en:
Alina Nazmeeva is a Tatarstan-born media artist, designer and educator working across physical installation, digital simulation, textile, and XR. With these diverse media, her practice builds complex worlds that investigate how technologies - emerging and established - shape, and are shaped by, situated spatial, social, and ecological practices.
Her work has been exhibited internationally, including at the Venice Biennale of Architecture, the Architecture + Design Museum in Los Angeles, the Beall Center for Art + Technology, and in major art and design festivals such as DA Z (Zurich), Slamdance (Los Angeles), HKWalls (Hong Kong), Collectible NYC, Collectible Brussels, and Alcova Milano. She has presented at Harvard GSD, UMPRUM, Parsons, Shanghai Institute of Visual Art, Seoul National University, Duke University, SIGGRAPH and ISEA. Her writing has appeared in Plat, Voices (Towards Other Institutions), Media-N, and AD (forthcoming).
Alina is Assistant Professor of Computation at the Illinois School of Architecture at UIUC. She holds a Master’s degree from MIT SA+P and has held fellowships at the University of Michigan (2022–24), the Canadian Centre for Architecture (2022), and the Strelka Institute (2017). She has held residencies at Art OMI & Monira Foundation (ongoing).
artist_bio_cn: Alina Nazmeeva 是出生于鞑靼斯坦的媒体艺术家，以模拟作为媒介与批判场域。她现任 UIUC 计算方向助理教授，作品曾在威尼斯建筑双年展、洛杉矶建筑与设计博物馆、Beall Center 和 Slamdance 等展出。她曾在 Art Omi、密歇根大学、加拿大建筑中心和 Strelka Institute 驻留，并曾在 Harvard GSD、Duke University、Parsons、ISEA、SIGGRAPH 等机构与会议发表作品。

description_en:
Mother’s Body Remembers presents an intimate visceral reality (VR) family portrait that examines memory, care, and the evolving conditions of presence within contemporary digital culture. The work originates from a simple yet charged gesture, an embrace between the artist and his aging mother, undertaken in anticipation of her declining mobility due to chronic illness. Holding this pose for ten minutes, both subjects confront vulnerability, distance, and the rediscovery of closeness, transforming stillness into a space of emotional and temporal intensity.

Using LiDAR technology, the artist captures this moment as a three-dimensional scan, preserving not only form but the affective resonance embedded within the act. The resulting data is subsequently translated into layered virtual brushstrokes, where the artist meticulously traces and repaints the merged bodies in VR. This process foregrounds digital craftsmanship as an embodied and durational practice, where gestures of care, touching, tracing, and re-encountering the maternal body, become integral to the work’s construction. Through this re-engagement, the artist becomes acutely aware of physical traces of aging, including fragility, imperfection, and subtle shifts in the body’s surface, prompting the re-emergence of childhood memories tied to tactile intimacy.

Motifs of osmanthus (桂花, Guihua), sharing the name of the artist’s mother, are woven throughout the composition as a symbolic and metaphysical bridge between memory, identity, and cultural inheritance. Accompanied by an audio layer of a lullaby once sung by the mother, the work extends into a multi-sensory archive of familial remembrance.

Challenging conventional two-dimensional modes of documentation, Mother’s Body Remembers proposes XR as a medium for living archives, where memory is not merely preserved but continually reactivated. Within a broader Singaporean context shaped by multilingual and multicultural histories, the work reflects on how emerging technologies may reconfigure legacy-making, sustaining relational presence across time, absence, and possible futures.
description_cn:
《母亲之身，记忆之所》（Mother’s Body Remembers）呈现了一件亲密的“内化实境”（Visceral Reality，VR）家庭肖像作品，探讨记忆、照护以及当代数字文化中“在场性”的演变。作品源于一个简单却富有张力的动作，艺术家与逐渐衰老的母亲之间的一次拥抱，发生于母亲因慢性疾病而行动能力逐步衰退之前。两人在此姿态中静止十分钟，在脆弱与距离之中重新感知亲密，使静止转化为情感与时间高度凝聚的场域。

艺术家通过 LiDAR 技术对这一瞬间进行三维扫描，不仅记录身体形态，也保留了其中蕴含的情动共振。随后，这些数据被转化为层叠的虚拟笔触，艺术家在 VR 中细致地描摹并重绘交叠的身体形态。该过程凸显了数字工艺作为一种具身且具时间性的实践方式，其中触碰、描绘与再次感知母体的动作，构成作品生成的核心机制。在这一再度接触之中，艺术家逐渐察觉到母亲身体中衰老的痕迹，包括脆弱、不完美以及皮肤表面的细微变化，并由此唤起与触觉经验相关的童年记忆。

作品中反复出现的桂花（Guihua）意象，与艺术家母亲的名字相呼应，成为连接记忆、身份与文化传承的象征性与形而上桥梁。伴随其间的音频层为母亲曾吟唱的摇篮曲，使作品延展为一处多感官的家庭记忆档案。

通过挑战传统二维影像的记录方式，《母亲之身，记忆之所》提出 XR 作为“活的档案”媒介的可能性，使记忆不仅被保存，更在持续生成与激活之中。在新加坡多语言与多文化交织的语境下，作品进一步反思新兴技术如何重塑“传承”的方式，使关系性的在场得以跨越时间、缺席与未来持续存在。
artist_bio_en:
Benedict Yu is a Visceral Reality (VR) artist, mixed-reality educator, and affective/quantum reality researcher whose practice operates at the intersection of art, technology, heritage, and spirituality. Based between Singapore and Berlin, his work interrogates the ontological, affective, and relational conditions of digital environments, positioning them as sites of embodied perception, speculative narration, and psychosocial restoration. Engaging transdisciplinary methodologies that bridge artistic production with critical inquiry, Yu situates his practice within broader discourses on posthumanism, affect theory, and expanded notions of materiality.

Central to his research is the development of Visceral Quantum Reality (VQR), a conceptual and practice-based framework that reconfigures digital space as an active field of co-creation, where self-generated healing, energetic awareness, and relational entanglements unfold across human and ecological systems. In this regard, his work challenges representational paradigms of virtuality, instead foregrounding immersion, embodiment, and participatory sense-making as critical modalities of knowledge production.

Yu’s works have been exhibited internationally and are held in major public and private collections, including Mapletree Investments Singapore, Mediacorp Singapore, the Paris Courtois Collection, GAW Capital, and Fondazione Opera Campana dei Caduti. His projects have been presented at key cultural institutions such as National Gallery Singapore, National Museum of Singapore, Asian Civilisations Museum, SomoS Berlin, and Zwölf Apostel Kirche Berlin, situating his practice within both contemporary art discourse and emergent XR ecologies.

In 2026, Yu serves as XR Development Lead for the National Arts Council Singapore’s Arts x Tech Lab, contributing to the advancement of extended reality as both a research medium and public cultural interface. Alongside his artistic practice, he is an active educator and speaker, contributing to academic discourse at the National University of Singapore and the University of the Arts Singapore (LASALLE/NAFA).
artist_bio_cn:
Benedict Yu 是一位“内化实境”（Visceral Reality）艺术家、混合现实教育者及情动／量子现实研究者，其实践位于艺术、科技、文化遗产与精神性之间的交汇领域。现往返于新加坡与柏林之间，他的创作从本体论、情动性与关系性层面出发，探讨数字环境的生成条件，将其视为具身感知、推测性叙事与心理修复的实践场域。通过跨学科方法，将艺术创作与批判性研究相结合，Yu 的实践与后人类主义、情动理论以及扩展物质性等理论话语形成对话。

其研究核心在于“内化量子实境”（Visceral Quantum Reality [VQR]）的建构——这一兼具概念性与实践性的框架，将数字空间重新理解为一种动态的共创场域，在其中，自我生成的疗愈、能量感知以及跨个体与生态系统的关系纠缠得以展开。在此语境下，他的创作超越了对虚拟性的再现性理解，转而强调沉浸、具身体验与参与式意义生成作为知识生产的关键机制。

Yu 的作品曾于国际范围内展出，并被多个重要公共及私人收藏机构收藏，包括新加坡丰树投资（Mapletree Investments）、新传媒（Mediacorp）、法国 Paris Courtois 收藏、香港基汇资本（GAW Capital）以及意大利 Fondazione Opera Campana dei Caduti。其项目亦曾于新加坡国家美术馆、新加坡国家博物馆、亚洲文明博物馆、柏林 SomoS 艺术空间及 Zwölf Apostel 等机构呈现，使其创作同时嵌入当代艺术语境与新兴 XR 生态之中。

2026年，Yu 担任新加坡国家艺术理事会“艺术与科技实验室”（Arts x Tech Lab）XR发展负责人，推动扩展现实作为研究媒介与公共文化界面的发展。除艺术实践外，他亦为活跃的教育者与讲者，于新加坡国立大学 (NUS) 及新加坡艺术大学（LASALLE／NAFA）参与教学与学术交流，持续拓展艺术、科技与具身数字经验的跨领域讨论。

artist_en: Ziwen Meng, Wei Song, Jie Yang, Shuo Zhang
artist_cn: 孟子文，宋玮， 杨洁， 张硕
description_en:
My Flower is a VR serious game designed to foster empathy for people living with Alzheimer’s disease (AD). From the patient’s subjective perspective, it constructs a dual-world narrative of “dream vs. reality”. Players travel between the two worlds to complete tasks, only to confront the harsh truth behind their actions: what they believed to be creation was actually unconscious smearing; what they thought was a search was aimless rummaging caused by memory loss; and the “enemy” they feared was their worried daughter.
Rather than merely educating about the disease, the game uses embodied interaction and narrative reversal to restore the real dilemmas faced by AD patients in cognitive confusion, challenging common misunderstandings of their behaviors. It conveys the core message that “memory may fade, but love does not disappear”, allowing players to understand and empathize with the real situation of Alzheimer’s patients through a first-person experience.
description_cn:
《My Flower》是一款聚焦阿尔茨海默症（AD）共情体验的 VR 严肃游戏，以患者的主观视角构建 “梦境 — 现实” 双重叙事。玩家将在两个世界中穿梭完成任务，待全部任务结束后，直面行为背后的真相：所谓的创作，是无意识的污渍涂抹；所谓的追寻，是记忆衰退后的徒劳翻找；所谓的敌人，是始终担忧自己的女儿。
      游戏并非单纯科普病症，而是通过具身交互与叙事反转，还原 AD 患者在认知混乱下的真实困境，打破大众对患者行为的刻板误解，传递 “记忆会消失，但爱不会” 的核心寓意，让玩家在第一人称体验中，真正理解并共情阿尔茨海默症患者的处境。
artist_bio_en:
Ziwen Meng: Multimedia Artist, focuses on multi-media artistic creation across diverse forms including digital media, service design and interactive installations, and committed to human-centered creative expression.
Wei Song: Focuses on the integration of art and engineering, virtual reality, augmented reality and human-computer interaction, and creates related digital artworks.
Jie Yang: Focuses on color science, color information interaction, color psychology, digital media and immersive experience research. Has participated in many major cultural and artistic events in Beijing and across China in recent years.
Shuo Zhang: Focuses on AI interactive imagery and VR image technology. Has created numerous digital images and art installation works.
artist_bio_cn:
孟子文，多媒体艺术创作者，专注于多媒介艺术创作，涉及数字媒体、服务设计、交互装置等多元载体，坚持以人为中心的创作表达。
宋玮，专注于艺工融合、虚拟现实、增强现实、人机交互等领域，并进行相关数字艺术作品创作。
杨洁，专注于色彩科学、色彩信息交互、色彩心理学、数字媒体与沉浸式体验研究等领域，近年来参与多项中国与北京大型文化与艺术活动。
张硕，专注于AI交互影像，VR影像技术领域，曾创作多项数字影像，艺术装置作品。

title_cn: Respire 2.0 沉浸式互动 VR 作品
artist_en: Artistic Directors: Philippe Pasquier, Mirjana Prpa, Katerina Semenko 3D Artist: Katerina Semenko Interaction Design: Mirjana Prpa Programmer: Szeka Tse Research Assistant: Dhruv Adhia Audio: Philippe Pasquier, Keon Leigh, Ge Liu
artist_cn: 艺术总监：Philippe Pasquier、Mirjana Prpa、Katerina Semenko；3D 艺术家：Katerina Semenko；交互设计：Mirjana Prpa；程序：Szeka Tse；研究助理：Dhruv Adhia；声音：Philippe Pasquier、Keon Leigh、Ge Liu
description_en:
Background
The original Respire established breath as a meaningful mode of interaction within virtual reality. Respire 2 builds on this foundation but deepens the experience: rather than navigating through external abstracted worlds, it situates the participant inside a lung-like interior, shifting the metaphor from observing environments to inhabiting the body itself. It expands the interaction vocabulary by introducing gestural hand movements and reconceives the sound layer as a co-breathing acoustic presence—moving the work toward a more open, reflective, and embodied encounter with breath.

System Design
Respire 2 is an immersive interactive artwork that transforms breathing into a spatial and sensory act. The experience unfolds inside an abstract, lung-like environment that responds to the participant’s presence. Breath functions as the primary mode of navigation. As the participant inhales and exhales, the virtual space subtly draws them closer into the lung, creating a sensation of entering an internal body. The rhythm and depth of breathing influence proximity, allowing the space to feel responsive and alive.

Sound emerges in parallel with breath, forming a living acoustic layer that expands and contracts with respiration. Rather than acting as feedback, sound behaves as a co-breathing element—shifting textures that mirror the participant’s internal rhythms. Gestural interaction introduces an additional bodily dialogue. Lateral hand movements allow participants to explore different regions of the lung, while a pushing gesture creates distance from the body’s interior. This interplay between breath-driven attraction and gesture-driven distancing creates a negotiation between surrender and agency.

Purpose
Respire 2 investigates breath as an expressive force. The work invites participants to experience breathing as a way of being in space—one that is intimate and deeply embodied. By situating the participant inside a responsive environment, the piece collapses distinctions between self and space. The act of breathing becomes visible and audible as presence.
description_cn: 《Respire》是一件沉浸式虚拟现实（VR）雕塑，连接数字艺术与人体生理之间的距离。作品呈现一个 3D 有机结构，并通过实时数据使其“苏醒”：传感器会追踪观众的呼吸。当使用者呼吸时，数字雕塑会以同步的光与运动映射这些生物节律，从而形成一种强烈的反馈循环。通过将无形的呼吸过程可视化，《Respire》探索内在自我的边界，以及技术在身体与数字环境之间建立深层、冥想式连接的潜力。
artist_bio_en:
Philippe Pasquier is a Professor at SFU’s School of Interactive Arts + Technology and director of the Metacreation Lab for Creative AI. A scientist-artist with 200+ publications, his work in generative systems and human-AI co-creation has been showcased at the Centre Pompidou, Ars Electronica, and the Sydney Biennale.

Dr. Mirjana Prpa is an Assistant Professor at HKUST (GZ) specializing in the intersection of AI, HCI, and Extended Reality. An award-winning researcher (ACM CHI Best Paper), she focuses on human-centered technology design for health, well-being, and experiential augmentation.

Katerina Semenko is an independent multidisciplinary phygital artist and conceptual designer bridging mixed reality and 3D hybrid digital sculptures, Winner of 30+ awards, including IDA Design of the Year, A’Design Gold, and James Dyson Award. Collaborates with global universities and top brands.

Programmer: Szeka Tse

Keon Ju Maverick Lee is a sound artist and Ph.D. candidate at SFU specializing in interactive music systems and AI-driven percussion performance. His work in human-AI collaboration has been showcased at premier venues including MUTEK Montréal, Ars Electronica, and SIGGRAPH.

Ge Liu is a game designer and composer with five years of industry experience, specializing in the intersection of sound design and game ludology. Currently a researcher at the Metacreation Lab for Creative AI (SFU), he focuses on generative music and pushing the boundaries of interactive audio experiences.

Dhruv Adhia is a human-centered technologist and creative systems thinker with over 15 years of experience driving innovation in XR, generative AI, and spatial computing through various CTO and advisory roles.
artist_bio_cn: Philippe Pasquier 是 SFU 教授及 Metacreation Lab 主任，作为科学家兼艺术家发表 200 余篇论文，作品曾在蓬皮杜中心和 Ars Electronica 展出。Mirjana Prpa 博士是香港科技大学（广州）助理教授，研究 AI、人机交互与以人为中心的 XR 设计，并曾获 ACM CHI 奖项。Katerina Semenko 是独立 phygital 艺术家与设计师，曾获 IDA Design of the Year、A'Design Award 等 30 余项荣誉。团队还包括提供技术支持的程序员 Szeka Tse、研究 AI 驱动打击乐的 SFU 博士候选人 Keon Ju Maverick Lee、研究生成音乐的 SFU 研究者与游戏作曲家 Ge Liu，以及拥有 15 年以上 XR 与空间计算经验的创意技术专家 Dhruv Adhia。

artist_en: Wang Lei, Wang Yi, Danqi Zheng, Duan Wenkai, Zhang Zige, Youchun Liu
artist_cn: 王雷，王漪，郑丹琪，段雯锴，张自歌，刘幼春
description_en:
The Cat Ghost is an 8-minute animated VR film. With a unique visual style from the ancient mural in the 2nd century, the film tells a story about the relationship between Chinese people and cats from the Western world. It is also a story about innocence defeating sophistication and love defeating suspicion.

One day, a white cat is presented from the Western countries to the Chinese emperor Wu. Fu Ling, the little son of the emperor, always being neglected by his father working all day, accidentally loses the cat in the cage. The cat makes a huge mess in the palace. Emperor Wu thinks the animal a bad omen and going to hurt people. He orders the guard to capture the cat and the shamans to cast spells. Eventually, Wu finds the truth about the animal with the help of his little son.
The film uses a traditional frame-by-frame 2D animation technique in virtual space to tell a story from 2nd-century China. Multiple elements, including lighting, animation performance, and sound, are used to guide the audience's center of interest.
description_cn: 短片讲述了公元2世纪，中国人与来自西方世界的猫之间发生的有趣故事。在VR空间中，创作团队通过传统的逐帧2D动画技术，创新性地融入了我国古代壁画视觉风格，尤其融入参考了敦煌壁画独具特色的艺术元素，使用灯光、动画表演和声音等多种元素，引导观众的注意力跟随剧情发展不变化，主动探索空间中的多样化表达。
artist_bio_en:
Lei Wang is a Professor and Dean of the School of Animation and Digital Art at the Communication University of China. A renowned director and screenwriter, his works have earned recognition in nearly 100 international festivals, including 20 Oscar-qualifying events. He leads DigiLab at CUC, an innovation hub established in 2023 to merge intelligent technologies with digital art, focusing on the contemporary expression of traditional culture.
Under his leadership, the lab produced China’s first AI-generated animation short, Dragon Gate, and large-scale immersive digital art exhibitions including Cats in the East (featuring The Cat Ghost) and The Splendid Qin Dynasty (featuring Glory of Qin: The First Chinese Dynasty). His practice integrates original content with technological innovation to redefine the boundaries of digital storytelling and immersive media, driving the evolution of digital art both domestically and internationally.
artist_bio_cn:
王雷，教授中国传媒大学动画与数字艺术学院院长，知名动画导演、编剧。其作品在近百个国际电影节和动画节中入围或获奖，包括中国文化艺术政府奖动漫奖。主创作品11次被国家广播电视总局推荐为优秀国产动画片。其代表作包括电视系列动画片《奇异虫洞》（导演、编剧）、《毛毛镇》系列（导演、编剧）、《叮叮咚咚毛毛镇》（编剧、制片人）、《毛毛镇冰雪运动队》（制片人、制片人）以及网络动画系列《云中三人组》（导演、编剧）等。

王雷教授带领的中国传媒大学DigiLab实验室于2023年成立，运用原创的数字技术与人工智能技术助力动画与数字艺术创作。实验室致力于打造一个集原创内容、技术创新和应用推广于一体的高水平创新平台，以艺术与技术的融合推动传统文化的当代表达。

王雷教授和实验室核心成员制作了中国首部AI生成动画短片《龙门》，《东方之猫》（2023年10月，北京）和《大秦风华》（2024年5月，咸阳）等大型沉浸式数字艺术展览，在动画和数字艺术领域获得国际认可。

artist_en: Soft Robotics - XRIM Labs (S.G. van Dipten, M.C. Chan, Y. C. Liang, C.K. Leung, K. Shatilov, R.B.N. Scharff, T. Braud)
artist_cn: 柔性机器人 — XRIM 实验室（S. G. van Dipten、陈鸣俊、梁宇辰、梁楚荞、Kirill Shatilov、沙博文教授、Tristan Braud 教授）
description_en:
The installation offers a soft-robot mediated handshake between the Hong Kong and Guangzhou campuses of HKUST. It combines a soft robotic hand designed to sense and replicate the feeling of a handshake with an extended reality networked system, placing two participants into the same virtual place, at the intersection between both campuses.

The soft robotic hand is a monolithic, MJF 3D-printed TPU interface with integrated sensing chambers and pneumatic actuators. To mediate wireless handshakes, an air pressure sensor captures the user's grip force. This data is processed by an STM32 microcontroller and transmitted via a Raspberry Pi using the MQTT protocol. The twin device receiving setup uses this signal to drive a proportional pressure valve, inflating their robotic hand to replicate the original grip force in real time.

The virtual reality experience was developed on Unity 6, using Meta avatar SDK for motion tracking together with a custom-built network stack for live retransmission of the motion. The system detects and aligns both sides of the experience dynamically to place the participants’ avatars in a shared virtual world centred around the physical robot hands location.
description_cn:
本装置通过软体机器人作为媒介，实现香港科技大学香港校区与广州校区之间的握手。它将一只能够感知并再现真实握手触感的软体机械手，与一个扩展现实网络系统相结合，使两名参与者置身于同一虚拟空间——该空间正位于两个校区的交汇处。
该软体机械手是一个一体化的、采用多射流熔融（MJF）3D打印技术制成的热塑性聚氨酯（TPU）界面，内部集成有感测腔室和气动执行器。为实现无线握手，一个气压传感器捕捉使用者的握力大小。这些数据由STM32微控制器进行处理，并通过树莓派（Raspberry Pi）利用MQTT协议进行传输。配对的另一侧设备收到信号后，驱动比例压力阀，为接收端的机械手充气，从而实时再现原始握力。
虚拟现实体验基于Unity 6开发，使用Meta Avatar SDK进行动作追踪，并采用自建的网络栈实时重传动作数据。系统动态检测并对齐体验双方的信号，将参与者的虚拟形象置于一个以实体机器人手位置为中心的共享虚拟世界中。
artist_bio_en:
The team was formed as a collaboration between Prof. Scharff and Prof. Braud’s teams at the HKUST Division of Integrative Systems and Design (ISD) to explore the intersection between soft robotics and remote presence. Members possess varied expertise across soft robotics, human-computer interaction, extended reality, and mechanical engineering.
Sweder van Dipten is a Ph.D. fellow at the HKUST Soft Robotics Lab specializing in human–robot interaction and computational design, with a focus on developing innovative soft robotic hands.
Ming Chun Chan is an ISD Ph.D. student whose research interests include soft robotics, embodied intelligence, and passive actuators.
Yuchen Liang holds B.Sc. and M.Phil. degrees from HKUST ISD and continues his Ph.D. research on soft bending actuators, artificial muscles, suction cups, and proprioception.
Cho Kiu Leung is an MPhil student in ISD. Her work focuses on the intersection of mechanical design and projection technology.
Kirill A. Shatilov earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from HKUST in 2026. His research focuses on natural human-computer interfaces, extended realities, and mobile computing.
Prof. Rob Scharff is an Assistant Professor in ISD. Previously a postdoctoral researcher at the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) with a Ph.D. from TU Delft, his research emphasizes the integrated design and manufacturing of bioinspired soft robots with proprioception and tactile sensing capabilities.
Prof. Tristan Braud is an Assistant Professor in ISD and director of the Extended Reality and Immersive Media Lab (XRIM Lab). With a Ph.D. from Université Grenoble Alpes, his research investigates interactive technologies with a focus on XR, and creative tools.
artist_bio_cn:
该团队由香港科技大学综合系统与设计学部（ISD）的沙博文教授（Prof. Rob Scharff）团队与 Prof. Tristan Braud 团队合作组建，旨在探索软体机器人与远程临场感的交叉领域。团队成员拥有广泛的专业背景，涵盖软体机器人、人机交互、扩展现实以及机械工程等领域。

Sweder van Dipten 是香港科技大学软体机器人实验室的博士研究员，专攻人机交互与计算设计，主要研究方向为创新型软体机械手。

陈鸣俊是综合系统与设计学部的博士生，研究兴趣包括软体机器人、具身智能以及被动执行器。

梁宇辰持有香港科技大学综合系统与设计学部的学士和哲学硕士学位，并继续攻读博士学位，研究方向为软体弯曲执行器、人工肌肉、吸盘与本体感知。

梁楚荞是综合系统与设计学部的哲学硕士生，其工作聚焦于机械设计与投影技术的交叉领域。

Kirill A. Shatilov 于 2026 年获得香港科技大学计算机科学与工程博士学位。他的研究集中在自然的人机交互界面、扩展现实及移动计算。

沙博文教授（Prof. Rob Scharff）是综合系统与设计学部的助理教授。他曾是意大利技术研究院（IIT）的博士后研究员，并在代尔夫特理工大学（TU Delft）获得博士学位。他的研究强调具有本体感知与触觉感知能力的仿生软体机器人的集成设计与制造。

Prof. Tristan Braud 是综合系统与设计学部的助理教授，同时担任扩展现实与沉浸式媒体实验室（XRIM Lab）主任。他在格勒诺布尔阿尔卑斯大学（UGA）获得博士学位，主要研究方向为交互技术、扩展现实及创意工具。

title_en: We Are The Primitives of a New Era
description_en:
We Are the Primitives of a New Era is a VR immersive work developed from Aldo Tambellini’s same-titled manifesto image and artistic vision first articulated in 1961. Conceived late in the artist’s life as his final creation, the project reinterprets that earlier declaration through contemporary immersive media, transforming a historic conceptual statement into a spatial audiovisual experience. Rather than presenting the original work as an object to be viewed at a distance, the piece invites the audience to enter a field of darkness, light, motion, sound, and language.

The work reflects Tambellini’s longstanding concern with the relationship between technological transformation and human consciousness. Its title proposes that we live in “a new era” in which invention and media do not simply extend perception, but reshape the conditions of being human. In this sense, the work is not nostalgic or retrospective. It treats immersion as a philosophical and perceptual condition, asking how art can translate cosmic force, inner perception, and collective uncertainty into sensory form. Tambellini’s enduring exploration of Black—as material, atmosphere, and metaphysical space—remains central here, carrying forward his broader language of projection, energy, and expanded cinema.

Technically, the project extends Tambellini’s intermedia practice into VR by combining immersive moving image with sound and a spatial logic rooted in his earlier installations, which brought together Black Film imagery, Lumagrams, projected poetry, and immersive environments. The result is a work that bridges historical avant-garde experimentation and contemporary immersive exhibition, preserving the radical spirit of Tambellini’s practice while giving it a new experiential form for present-day audiences. Public descriptions of the piece frame it through VR, immersive video, image, poetry, and sound rather than through AI-based generation, so its engagement with technology is better understood as a continuation of intermedia and immersive media traditions than as a generative AI artwork
description_cn: 《We Are the Primitives of a New Era》是一件 VR 沉浸式作品，将 Aldo Tambellini 1961 年基于宣言的项目重新诠释为空间化的视听环境。作品延续 Tambellini 长期以来对“黑色”、光、投影以及宇宙想象的探索，通过环绕观众的动态影像与声音，唤起一个人类感知正被太空时代与新技术前景重塑的时刻。作品并未将沉浸体验视为奇观，而是邀请观众思考艺术如何在身体与宇宙、黑暗与视觉、记忆与发明之间，调解人类面对未知时的感知与想象。
artist_bio_en:
Aldo Tambellini (1930–2020) was an Italian-American artist, poet, filmmaker, and one of the key pioneers of electronic intermedia, expanded cinema, and early video art. Born in Syracuse, New York, and raised in Lucca, Italy, he studied painting at Syracuse University and later earned an MFA in sculpture from the University of Notre Dame. Across more than six decades, he worked across painting, sculpture, film, poetry, performance, and television, consistently pushing against the boundaries between media and redefining what art could become in the electronic age.

A central thread in Tambellini’s practice was his sustained exploration of Black—not only as a color, but as a philosophical, political, and spatial condition. His celebrated bodies of work, including Black Zero, Black TV, Lumagrams, and later multimedia installations, brought together moving image, light, sound, and live performance to address race, technology, social upheaval, and inner perception. In 1960s New York, he was deeply involved in the experimental downtown art scene and, with Otto Piene, co-founded the Black Gate Theatre, now widely recognized as a foundational site for expanded media and early video installation.

Tambellini’s work has been presented internationally at major institutions and exhibitions including Tate Modern, MoMA, Centre Pompidou, ZKM, and the Venice Biennale. His legacy continues to shape contemporary media art through its fusion of artistic experimentation, technological inquiry, and political urgency. This presentation is produced by Topos Studio, a Seoul-based immersive media studio founded in 2019 by researchers from the University of Aberdeen. As a creative studio and curatorial incubator, Topos Studio collaborates with artists to translate their works into immersive exhibition formats for contemporary audiences
artist_bio_cn: Aldo Tambellini（1930-2020）是一位意大利裔美国艺术家，也是电子跨媒介、扩展电影与早期录像艺术的先驱。他的实践横跨绘画、雕塑、电影、诗歌、表演与电视，并围绕“黑色”作为材料与思想发展出激进的视觉语言。20 世纪 60 年代，他活跃于纽约实验艺术现场，曾与 Otto Piene、Nam June Paik 等艺术家合作，作品后来在泰特现代美术馆、MoMA、蓬皮杜中心和威尼斯双年展等重要机构展出。他的创作将艺术、技术与政治紧迫感结合起来，对媒体艺术产生了持久影响。

title_en: What is it like to be a memory
title_cn: 作为记忆是什么样的体验？
description_en: In the quiet, haunting expanse of a German winter, "What is it like to be a memory?" invites you into a liminal, surreal landscape captured through 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). This immersive experience transforms a physical environment into a "Dreamcore" world, a space that feels both familiar and deeply nostalgic, yet fundamentally unmoored from reality.  As you navigate this frozen, quiet cityscape, the boundaries between you and the environment dissolve. Using the Gemini Live API for low-latency voice interaction, you engage in a conversational dialogue with the space itself. Every movement and word shapes the experience, from voice-controlled locomotion to gestures that guide the flight of surreal, steampunk insects that hover in the snowy air.  Accompanied by an ethereal score composed with Suno, this artwork explores the nature of memory, its persistence, its fragility, and its quiet beauty. It is a world suspended in a perpetual snow, a reflection of the moments that linger, just beyond our reach.   Technical & Creative Details Interaction: Fully conversational, "controller-less" 3D experience using voice and hand tracking.  Integration: Unity + Gemini Live API, with the Gemini Unity integration open source here: https://git.informatik.uni-hamburg.de/presence/public/iva-sdk-core-public  Tech Stack: PCVR (Quest 3 via Quest Link) powered by an RTX 5070Ti laptop for a smooth, high-resolution experience.  Musical Composition: Background score created with Suno and triggered by Gemini at approporiate context using function calling capability.
description_cn:
在德国冬日的幽静旷野中，《作为记忆是什么样的体验？》通过 3D高斯泼溅技术 (3DGS) 打造了一个名为“梦核”（Dreamcore）的超现实阈限空间。这种沉浸式体验将物理环境转化为一个既令人感到怀旧，又彻底脱离了现实的奇异场域。

当你穿行于这片冰封的城景，通过AI驱动的对话与手势交互，你将直接与环境本身展开交流，并指引蒸汽朋克昆虫在雪中起舞。伴随着 Suno 创作的空灵配乐，本作品探讨了记忆的脆弱与持久。这是一个悬浮在永恒落雪中的世界，映射着那些徘徊在触及之外、如影随形的瞬息之美。

展览说明： 本次展出版本采用预录制的AI对话及同步视觉特效，以确保在无需云端连接的情况下，依然能为观众提供流畅、高保真的沉浸式体验。
artist_bio_en:
cocolinux is a technical artist and mixed reality researcher based in Hamburg, Germany, working at the intersection of immersive media and cutting-edge rendering technologies. Her artistic practice focuses on bringing the dreamcore aesthetic to spatial computing, utilizing the latest advancements in generative world models and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Through her visual effects, she seeks to trigger anemoia, a profound sense of nostalgia for times and spaces that never actually existed. Her dreamcore piece, Snow After Us, was awarded third place at the inaugural World Labs Winter Competition in 2026.

Beyond her personal artwork, cocolinux bridges the gap between research and practical development. She created the first commercially adopted 3DGS shader and VFX toolkit for Unity. Featuring advanced volumetric relighting, this toolkit currently supports over 150 studios and independent developers worldwide. In academia, her research on radiance field rendering, spatial interactions, and intelligent virtual agents is frequently published at top international venues like TVCG, ISMAR, IEEE VR, and IROS. She also actively contributes to the XR research community, serving on the international program committees for premier conferences, including IEEE VR 2026 and ISMAR 2026.

artist_bio_cn:
cocolinux 是一位常驻德国汉堡的技术美术与混合现实研究员，主要在沉浸式媒体与前沿渲染技术的交汇处进行探索。她的艺术实践侧重于将梦核美学引入空间计算领域，并结合生成式世界模型与3D高斯泼溅（3DGS）的最新技术进展。通过视觉特效的创作，她希望能触发一种名为“anemoia”的情感共鸣，即对从未真实存在过的时空所产生的怀旧感。2026年，其梦核主题作品《Snow After Us》在首届 World Labs 冬季竞赛中获得了季军。

在个人创作之外，cocolinux 也致力于将技术研究转化为实际应用。她开发了首个投入商业使用的、适用于Unity的3DGS着色器与视觉特效工具包。该工具包具备高级体积重光照功能，目前有幸为全球150多家工作室和独立开发者提供技术支持。在学术领域，她关于辐射场渲染与交互以及虚拟智能体的研究工作，曾多次发表于 TVCG、ISMAR、IEEE VR 和 IROS 等国际重要学术会议与期刊。此外，她也积极参与学术界的服务工作，在 IEEE VR 2026 和 ISMAR 2026 等相关领域的重要学术会议中担任国际程序委员会委员。
